messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: MatlabStan dump format problem
parts:
Although I found this when using MatlabStan, this might affect other interfaces using CmdStan and dump format.

A following model

data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  real Y[N];
} 
parameters {
  real mu; 
} 
model {
  Y ~ normal(mu, 1);
} 

works with the following data dump file
N <- 2
Y <- c(1)

but not with the following
N <- 2
Y <- 1

The latter dump file is generated by MatlabStan because Matlab does not make difference between a scalar and 1x1 vector. If Y has more than element in Matlab, the MatlabStan creates correct dump file. We can't change MatlabStan to dump all scalars as c(.), since CmdStan does not accept that for a scalar type.

Would it be possible that CmdStan would accept a scalar value for a vector with length 1 or matrix with size 1x1?

Aki

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] MatlabStan dump format problem
parts:
That is a feature, not a bug!

Did you mean to have

N <- 1

? I don't see how it'd work with N <- 2, because
Y is only size 1 array/vector.

Unlike R, Stan distinguishes between arrays and
scalars. One of the reasons R is so inefficient is
that it just converts them freely back and forth. It's
also a potential source of bugs, because not checking
types can mask programming errors.

I strongly prefer types to be explicit, which is why
Stan's designed how it is. I expected WAY more pushback
on this from the statisticians than we've gotten, which
makes me very happy.

- Bob
